title: Hub capability document
description: What a hub (Nightscout, Nocturne) supports for controller registrations, published unauthenticated at `/.well-known/nightscout/sync` on every host the hub serves (D18 addendum rule 6, execution plan §2.6.1; specified by queue item SPEC-REG-NEGOTIATE). A controller reads it before submitting a registration and can compute from it which elements the hub would accept (tools/nsschema/negotiate.py is the reference for that computation); the submit response is authoritative. The document describes the hub software and the deployment, never a person: it lists the hub-shipped well-known kinds and none of the registrations a tenant's controllers have submitted, because which controller a person uses is not public. Must-ignore applies here as in the grammar: no object is closed, and a reader ignores members it does not know. An unknown value of a closed list is invalid; `grammar.versions[].apiVersion` and the vocabularies below are closed so a controller can rely on them.

apiVersion.description: The version of this document's own shape. Within v1 a reader ignores members it does not know.

hub.description: Informational. A controller must not branch on the product or version; it reads the capability members below instead.

grammar.description: Which registration grammar versions the hub reads, and which grammar members it interprets.

versions.description: One entry per grammar major the hub reads. A registration whose `apiVersion` is not listed is rejected whole (`unsupported-grammar-major`). The minor is the grammar revision the hub implements within that major; a registration carries no minor, because within a major the hub ignores members it does not know (rule 1).

interprets.description: The grammar members the hub interprets, as dotted member paths of the registration with `*` for an array item or a map key (`spec.stateSpans.*.wire`, `spec.extensions`). An entry covers the member and everything beneath it. A member of a submitted registration that no entry covers is ignored: kept as written, not interpreted, not served as data, and listed in the response's `ignored`. A member the grammar does not define is ignored whatever this list says. The list must cover the members the submit contract itself reads (`apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata.vendor`, `metadata.product`, `metadata.tier`, `spec.cadence`, `spec.documents.*.collection`, `spec.documents.*.decomposesTo`); tools/nsschema/negotiate.py `capability_problems` checks that, because coverage by prefix cannot be stated in JSON Schema.

horizons.description: Rule 5. The horizon classes and availability values the hub stores. A kind, extension or typed field that declares a class or availability not listed here is rejected as an element (`unsupported-horizon`, `unsupported-availability`), and the controller writes its well-known carrier. Absent: the hub stores none of the declared horizons and supports `released` only.

typeFragment.description: Rule 2. The subset of the grammar's type-fragment keywords the hub can store, validate and index. A typed field (extension field, `settings.fields[]`, `replayInputs[]`) whose `type`, or whose `typeRef` target, uses a keyword or format outside this subset is rejected as an element (`unsupported-type-keyword`): the hub never accepts a constraint it would not apply. Must be a subset of the grammar's own fragment keywords.

formats.description: The `format` values the hub supports. Absent with `format` in `keywords`: every grammar format.

limits.description: Bounds the hub enforces. `maxRegistrationBytes` (the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the submitted registration) and `maxExtensions` reject the whole registration; `maxFieldsPerExtension` and `maxTypeDepth` (nesting of `items`/`properties`, a scalar type being depth 1) reject the element. Absent: no stated limit.

wellKnown.description: The well-known tier (D18): registrations the hub ships, generated from measurement, which describe today's writers with no controller change. Served at the controller-descriptions catalogue (`/.well-known/nightscout/controllers`, PROPOSAL-controller-descriptions §2.1).

catalogue.description: The catalogue index, as a path on this host.

href.description: The well-known registration, as a path on this host.

submit.description: Where a controller submits a controller-owned registration (specs/sync/registration-submit.schema.json). Absent: the hub does not accept submissions, for example while a hub's feature flag is off, and every element falls back to its well-known carrier.

href.description: The registrations collection, as a path on this host. One registration is the resource `<href>/<vendor>/<product>`, each segment percent-encoded.

tiers.description: The tiers a controller may submit. Only `controller-owned`: the well-known tier ships with the hub.

permissions.description: The permissions a credential needs, so a controller can tell an operator what to grant. Proposed names; see the open questions in the hub-sync design §3.5.

instances.description: D19 (execution plan §2.6.2; SPEC-REG-INSTANCE; hub-sync design §3.6). Present: the hub stores definitions at `<submit.href>/<vendor>/<product>/definitions/<definitionId>` and instances at `<submit.href>/<vendor>/<product>/instances/<instanceId>`, and requires an instance id on every typed write (an instance-less typed write is refused `instance-required`, a definite refusal, so that record goes as its carrier). Writes with no instance — older controllers and the well-known tier — are attributed to an implicit unregistered instance of the product and never refused for exclusivity. Absent: the hub takes neither resource and typed writes need no instance (SPEC-REG-NEGOTIATE as it stands). A controller reads this at launch and after a controller release, never on a lease renewal (decision 8).

leaseSeconds.description: Rule 4. How long an instance's lease runs from each create or renewal; `leaseExpiresAt` in each response is that time. An instance that does not renew lapses: it holds no roles, and a role it held is granted to a claimant on the claimant's next renewal, never automatically.

instanceId.description: The instance id form the hub accepts: a random lowercase UUID version 4 (122 random bits). Absent means `uuid-v4`.

roles.description: Rule 5. The roles the hub grants: the shared `source` and `command-sink`, and any `{value: other, controllerTerm}` it knows. A role not listed is refused `unsupported-role`. Every listed role is exclusive among live `device`-provenance instances (rule 6).

channels.description: Rule 5. The channel forms the hub derives from a definition: `slot`, the slot name a stateSpans kind declares (shared across products on the tenant); `element`, `<vendor>/<product>/<element id>` for every other element. Closed: a form outside the list is invalid.

labels.description: Rule 7. Bounds on an instance's labels; a label over them refuses the instance `invalid-label`. Absent: no stated bound.
